text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Australian politician JOHN LUCAS was born in 1818. He was a campaigner against public waste and was the man who opened the Jenolan Caves.

American heavyweight boxing champion JACK (WILLIAM HARRISON) DEMPSEY was born in 1895. Nicknamed the "Manassa Mauler", DEMPSEY beat JESS WILLARD for the title in 1919 and held it until 1926, when he lost it to GENE TUNNEY.
Argentine racing driver JUAN FANGIO was born in 1911.
UK drummer MICK FLEETWOOD, one of the original members of 'Fleetwood Mac', was born in 1942.
UK guitarist JEFF BECK was born in 1944. He took over from ERIC CLAPTON in the 'Yardbirds'. He was a very successful session musician and had his biggest solo hit with "Hi-Ho Silver Lining".
Australia's sprinter RAYLENE BOYLE, who won two silver medals at the Olympics and gold medals at two Commonwealth Games, was born in 1951.
UK trumpeter and announcer for UB40 ASTRO was born in 1957. His real name is TERENCE WILSON and he's usually the central figure in their stage shows.
** EVENTS **
1314 : ROBERT the BRUCE of Scotland inflicted a crushing
defeat against superior English forces under King EDWARD II at the battle of Bannockburn.
1509 : HENRY VIII was crowned King of England.
1519 : LUCREZIA BORGIA, Italian noblewoman and a member
of the infamous Borgia family of the Italian Renaissance, died.
1717 : The Grand Lodge of English freemasons began in
London.
1812 : NAPOLEON, leading his Grand Armee, began his
ill-fated invasion of Russia.
1901 : An exhibition of work by new young Spanish painter
PABLO PICASSO opened at a Paris gallery.
1916 : The First Battle of the Somme began. It lasted
five months and the death toll of over one million was for the sake of an allied advance of 125 square miles.
1940 : Japan formally asked Britain to close the Burma
Road into China.
1941 : The Germans advanced into Russia and took Vilna,
Brest-Litovsk and Kaunas.
1947 : An American pilot reported seeing strange objects
in the sky looking like "saucers skipping across the water". This incident led to the first use of the term "flying saucers".
1948 : The Berlin airlift began with the Allies flying
supplies of food into the city after the Soviet blockade.
1953 : The engagement of U.S. Senator JOHN F.KENNEDY to
JACQUELINE BOUVIER was announced.
1955 : In Kenya, nine Mau Mau terrorists were given death
sentences for murdering two English school boys.
1968 : British comedian TONY HANCOCK committed suicide in
a Sydney hotel room. He was one of the most popular entertainers in Britain during his long-running radio program "Hancock's Half Hour". The show transferred to television in 1956.
1973 : EAMON de VALERA, the world's oldest statesman,
resigned as president of Ireland at the age of 90.
1973 : The Cold War started to wane. Soviet leader LEONID
BREZHNEV ended a week-long trip to the United States. BREZHNEV and U.S President NIXON both hailed the visit as "a further milestone" in improving relations between the two super-powers.
1983 : America's first woman in space returned safely to
earth. SALLY RIDE, a 32-year-old physicist, was one of five crew members on board the space shuttle CHALLENGER.
1985 : Britain's longest surviving heart transplant
patient, KEITH CASTLE, died 6 years after receiving his donor heart.
1989 : ZHAO ZIYANG, who had expressed sympathy with
pro-democracy students, was replaced by JIANG ZEMIN as General Secretary of the Communist Party.
1990 : In Ireland, the first women priests were ordained
into the Anglican Church. The historic ceremony was conducted in St Anne's Cathedral in Belfast. The Bishop of Connor said the ordinations heralded a new era for the Church.
1994 : South Africa resumed its seat in the 184-nation
General Assembly of the United Nations, after a 20 year absence.
